subject: Renewal & expansion recap: usage, pain points, and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@finlytics.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@finlytics.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal & expansion recap: usage, pain points, and next steps

Hi Jared / Priya —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our renewal + expansion discussion and agreed next steps so we all have the same view. Please reply here if I missed anything.

Key takeaways (what we heard)
- Current usage: ~18M tokens/month across staging + production; peak daily QPS on chat endpoints ~420 reqs/min. (see attached usage CSV)
- Pain points: intermittent latency spikes during peak windows (~250-400ms 95p -> impacts UX), rising per-token cost for semantic search workload, and cache miss rate on long multi-turn sessions.
- New workloads: expanding semantic search (embeddings) + multi-turn assistant with 16k–32k context for knowledge work.
- Goal: keep end-user latency under 200ms p95 while reducing per-token cost by ~25% for search traffic.

Proposed upsell path / recommendation from Redwood
1) Pilot dedicated capacity: 2 reserved GPU instances (prod-only pool) for a 2-week performance & cost pilot. This addresses latency SLOs and gives predictable unit economics.
2) Quantization & batching profile: apply our mixed-precision profile for the search model to cut token cost; expect ~20–30% reduction depending on request shape.
3) Migration plan: staged rollout (canary -> 50% -> full) with automatic fallback to hosted model variants.
4) SLA & commercial: see attached draft SLA (redwood-sla-proposal.pdf). We can follow up to align terms in the next week.

Timeline / next steps
- Mar 3: Finlytics to confirm pilot acceptance and target traffic slice (~10% production / specific endpoint). -> Jared / Priya
- Mar 5: Redwood to provide pilot config and cost projection (Marissa + Logan). -> Marissa / Logan (I will share numbers by EOD Mar 4)
- Mar 9: Pilot kickoff call (logistics + runbook). -> Logan to schedule
- Mar 31: Decision on expansion / reserved commitment for Dedicated capacity. -> Finlytics execs

Attachments: 20260301-usage-report.csv, redwood-sla-proposal.pdf
Useful links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/54321 | DocuSign (estimate): https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/abc123

Open questions for you
- Can you confirm the traffic slice and the two search endpoints you want in pilot?
- Any data residency or SOC2 requirements beyond what we discussed? (we flagged SOC2 in the deck)

Thanks — happy to hop on a brief call if that’s easier to finalize.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@finlytics.com>

Date: 2026-03-02T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal & expansion recap: usage, pain points, and next steps

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Pilot traffic slice: we can start with ~12% of production on the semantic-search endpoint (/v1/search/sem) and the assistant endpoint (/v1/chat/assist). That should be a representative mix.
2) Cost reduction: before committing we want a short proof that moving to Dedicated + quantization gets us the ~25% reduction you mentioned. A two-week pilot with performance + cost metrics sounds fair.
3) Security / compliance: SOC2 Type II is required for our procurement — we do have SOC2 in place but would like to see the report and confirm data residency (US only) for the pilot data.

We'll confirm formally by EOD Mar 3. If you can include a simple expected cost-per-token projection and the pilot runbook that would help speed internal approval.

—Jared
